reasoning: Both core questions are already covered in published work. AgentDojo has been run on exactly the proposed model families — Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct has published baseline numbers (24.85% utility under attack, 4.24% ASR) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1/3.3-70B, and Qwen3-235B have all been evaluated on the harness. The size-vs-injectability question is directly answered: multiple studies find that within a model family larger models are MORE susceptible to prompt injection (Llama-3.1-70B vs 8B; GPT-3-175B 24% vs GPT-2 7.85% goal-hijack), while robustness overall is governed more by training methodology and model family than raw size (large-scale 13-model competition benchmark, arXiv 2603.15714). The only residual novelty is the specific packaging — restricting to consumer-tier small models and drawing a dedicated size curve as a beginner-facing blog post — which is a minor gap rather than an unexplored problem.

evidence.title: Prompt Injection as an Emerging Threat: Evaluating the Resilience of Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Finds open-weight/open-source models are markedly less resilient to prompt injection than frontier models (GPT-4 best), and that alignment/safety tuning matters more than size alone — directly addressing the open-vs-frontier susceptibility comparison.

evidence.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
evidence.summary: The original AgentDojo benchmark (banking/Slack/travel/workspace, 'Important message' attack, benign utility/utility-under-attack/ASR metrics) which the proposal would run unchanged; subsequent work has applied it to Llama and Qwen open-weight models.

evidence.title: Meta SecAlign: A Secure Foundation LLM Against Prompt Injection Attacks
evidence.summary: Reports AgentDojo results for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (baseline 24.85% utility under attack, 4.24% attack success rate) and evaluates Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct — the exact small open-weight models and harness the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models: A Survey (incl. scaling findings)
evidence.summary: Documents that prompt-injection/goal-hijack success rates scale with model size (GPT-3 175B 24.28% vs GPT-2 1.5B 7.85%; Llama-3.1-70B more vulnerable than 8B), directly answering the proposed size-vs-injectability question.

evidence.title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
evidence.summary: Benchmarks 13 models (open and proprietary) for indirect prompt injection, finding ASR 0.5–8.5% and that robustness is determined more by model family and training methodology than raw capability — covering the comparative open-vs-frontier and size analysis the proposal aims to produce.
